These documents claim sliders slow pages, push content below the fold, and are largely ignored by users, which undermines SEO. In contrast, a minority of sources contend that sliders need not harm SEO if implemented carefully, emphasizing accessibility, mobile responsiveness, and engagement benefits [d5][d7][d8]. They suggest that poorly built sliders can hurt SEO, but well-optimized ones may be neutral or even supportive via improved engagement. Because the evidence presents genuinely opposing viewpoints within the same scope and time window, there is no clear consensus on whether sliders are inherently bad for SEO.
